To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) children are interested in using digital libraries for writing; 2) children are interested to use a collaborative digital library environment for writing; 3) children are interested and capable of participating in the design of digital libraries for writing.
the children's digital library should be designed to be a collaborative writing space that is easy to use and provides the tools for children to write, edit, and share their work.

children are capable of engaging in the design process, that they are able to contribute to the design of a digital library, that they are capable of using a digital library, and that children are able to collaborate in writing stories and poems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
how we might support children to use digital libraries to create their own stories and poems, and the role that digital library design might play in this process.
how to design an engaging digital library environment to support collaborative writing for children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
children can be involved in the design process and that the design process can be successful.
the children were able to use the digital library effectively to support their collaborative story writing and that it was a positive experience for the children.

we have found that children are very enthusiastic about the prospect of designing a children's digital learning environment, that they are very willing to participate in the design process and that their contributions are of great value in designing an effective and engaging digital library environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
children's digital libraries should provide children with a safe and engaging environment in which they can learn and develop new skills and knowledge in an interactive, creative and fun way.
we have developed a prototype for a digital library that is designed with children, and that is designed to be used by children.

children can be engaged as design partners and can contribute valuable ideas and suggestions for the design of children's digital libraries, but that they may need some support in understanding the design process.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is important to engage children as design partners in the design of a children's digital environment, and to provide a collaborative writing environment that supports the development of children's writing skills.
it is important to engage children in the early design phases of digital library systems.
the digital library design process should be an iterative one, with children as partners throughout the design process.
